Kaful: from equipment manuals to remaining-life forecasts

Three machines, from their documents to probabilistic remaining-life forecasts, every number traceable.

  • Eversys: Calibrated but not sharp: on 2 observed quantities the particle_filter's 90% intervals hold the truth 94%-99% of the time (target 85%-95%, every interval consistent with it); alpha-lambda passes in 15 of 88 forecasts; the 95% point lies past the horizon in 23 of 24 top_piston_failure forecasts, 39 of 64 water_filter_failure forecasts.
  • CNC spindle: Calibrated but not sharp: on 1 observed quantity the particle_filter's 90% intervals hold the truth 88% of the time (target 85%-95%, every interval consistent with it); alpha-lambda passes in 0 of 33 forecasts, and the median 90% interval spans 1.9x the true RUL (0.62x open-loop's on the same forecasts).
  • Air compressor: Calibrated but not sharp: on 2 observed quantities the particle_filter's 90% intervals hold the truth 96%-100% of the time (target 85%-95%, every interval consistent with it); alpha-lambda passes in 3 of 47 forecasts, and the median 90% interval spans 1.1-2.5x the true RUL.

Absolute rates are checked for consistency with the documentation and physics, not for accuracy: without real failure data, no number here says how long a real part will last.

Calibration is scored on synthetic data generated from the twin's own ParamSet: a pipeline sanity check, partly circular, not validation.

Coverage of parts with no observation of their own (unobserved, or whose posterior equals the prior) is the prior predictive scored against truth drawn from that prior: circular by construction, reported separately.

1 · The pipeline

A machine's documents in, a twin and remaining-life forecasts out.

4 · Wear over time

Each part degrades by a physics-shaped template; documented maintenance resets it.

5 · Tracking a machine from its sensors

A particle filter updates each part's health and its own rate from the readings.

6 · Remaining-life forecasts

Forecasts at several issue times, against the true failure time.

every synthetic unit of this machine; F3 shows the one its rule picks

7 · Is the uncertainty honest?

Calibrated but not sharp.

8 · What if?

Forecasts under a changed maintenance plan.

9 · Cost

Every LLM call is logged, cached and priced.

10 · Not everything gets a physics model

Scope decides which parts get a full model before any expensive per-part work.
